name: Aurum Custody
tagline: Institutional custodial wallets and tokenized gold for Dubai and the EU
summary: Fictional VASP targeting Dubai VARA licensing and EU MiCA CASP/ART authorisation. Strong on wallet segregation and cold-storage policy; thin on complaints, reserve attestation, and market-abuse controls.

documents.title: Aurum Custody — Confidential Project Pack (White Paper excerpt)
documents.content:
AURUM CUSTODY  |  PROJECT PACK v0.9  |  CONFIDENTIAL
Target markets: Dubai (VARA) and the European Union (MiCA)
Prepared for internal licensing-gap review. Not an offering document.

1. Issuer and services
Aurum Custody FZE ("Aurum") is a virtual-asset service provider in formation. The firm intends to offer two tightly coupled products. First, institutional custodial wallets for bitcoin, ether, and a short list of ERC-20 tokens, marketed to family offices and gold-trading desks. Second, AURUM-X, a tokenized gold product in which each on-chain unit is described as representing a claim on allocated London Good Delivery gold held in a third-party vault. The commercial thesis is that the same legal entity can both issue AURUM-X and act as the on-chain custodian of client wallets that hold it. The founders have mapped the intended Dubai activities to VARA Custody Services and VA Issuance, and the intended EU activities to MiCA crypto-asset service provider (CASP) custody and administration of crypto-assets on behalf of clients, plus issuance of an asset-referenced token. No licence has been granted in either jurisdiction. A draft programme of operations exists as an internal slide deck; it has not been filed with a competent authority or with VARA.

2. Custody architecture and client-asset segregation
Aurum's custody design is the most mature part of the pack. Client virtual assets are never commingled with the firm's treasury. Each client is assigned a unique on-chain deposit address; credits are swept into a segregated omnibus cold vault whose keys are unknown to the trading and issuance desks. The cold vault is a 3-of-5 multi-party computation (MPC) scheme with two shards held by an independent key-ceremony vendor in Luxembourg, two shards in a Dubai HSMs under dual control, and one shard in offline CEO custody for disaster recovery only. Hot wallets are capped at 2% of aggregate client holdings and are rebalanced to cold storage at least once every 24 hours. A daily reconciliation job compares on-chain balances to the internal client ledger; breaks above 10 basis points escalate to the Head of Operations. The custody policy, titled "Aurum Client Asset Segregation and Wallet Inventory Standard", is a 19-page controlled document. It forbids rehypothecation or use of client assets for the firm's own account. Wallet inventory (hot/cold, client/firm, chain, address) is maintained in a signed CSV exported to the compliance share every business day. These arrangements are intended to meet the substance of MiCA custody and administration duties and the VARA Custody Services Rulebook segregation and key-management expectations.

3. Key management, access, and operational resilience (partial)
Key ceremonies are run against a written runbook. Privileged access to the MPC console requires hardware tokens and is logged. The firm has a one-page business-continuity note stating that if Dubai infrastructure fails, Luxembourg shards can reconstruct a spending quorum within 72 hours. There is no tested disaster-recovery exercise, no independent penetration test of the wallet stack, and no incident-response plan that names a VARA or EU competent-authority notification trigger. Outsourcing of the MPC vendor and the cloud observability stack is covered by unsigned MSA templates; there is no outsourcing register, no due-diligence file, and no documented exit plan if the key vendor fails.

4. AURUM-X — tokenized gold product
AURUM-X is presented as a fully reserved, allocated gold token. Marketing copy states that "every token is backed 1:1 by investment-grade gold." The backing description in this pack is a two-paragraph vault letter of intent from a Swiss warehouse, plus a founder-prepared spreadsheet listing bar serial numbers as of a single date last quarter. There is no independent attestation of quantity, quality, or segregation of the bars. There is no legal opinion on whether the token confers a proprietary claim on specific bars or a contractual claim on the issuer. Encumbrance is not addressed: the letter of intent is silent on liens. Redemption is described in a single sentence: "Institutional holders may request physical delivery subject to a 400 oz minimum and fees to be published." There is no operational playbook, no SLA, no liquidity plan if many holders redeem at once, and no public summary of reserve composition. The token is intended to be offered in both Dubai and the EU; the pack does not contain a MiCA Title III white paper with the prescribed headings, nor a VARA VA Issuance white paper. Risk factors occupy half a page and do not discuss de-peg, vault failure, or the conflict inherent in Aurum acting as both issuer and custodian of AURUM-X.

5. Disclosures and marketing
A landing-page draft promises "bank-grade custody" and "fully reserved gold, always." Fee language is incomplete ("competitive institutional rates"). There is no fee schedule, no regulatory-status statement, and no comparison of marketing claims against a filed white paper. The founders consider this pack itself to be the disclosure document.

6. Governance, conflicts, and prudential
Aurum currently has two co-founders (CEO and CTO) and a part-time legal adviser. There is no board charter, no appointed Compliance Officer, and no MLRO. A one-slide organisational chart shows "Compliance — TBD." Conflicts of interest are not documented, despite the obvious dual role of issuer and custodian of AURUM-X and the fact that the CEO would hold both a residual interest in the issuance SPV and control of disaster-recovery key material. Related-party dealings (the MPC vendor is a former employer of the CTO) are undisclosed. Paid-up capital is described as "seed funding in process." There is no own-funds calculation against MiCA Art. 67 minima, no VARA activity-category capital table, and no professional-indemnity or cyber insurance binder.

7. Complaints, consumer protection, and client handling
The pack contains no complaints-handling procedure, no published channel, no SLA, and no register. Support is described as "Telegram for launch partners." There is no fair-treatment policy, no vulnerable-client standard, and no plan to offer a free-of-charge complaints route in an official language of an EU home Member State or in Arabic for Dubai clients. This section is a known drafting gap; the legal adviser flagged it in comments and it has not been closed.

8. Market abuse and conduct
AURUM-X is expected to trade on at least one third-party platform after launch. The pack has no market-abuse policy, no insider list, no wall-crossing procedure, no surveillance arrangement, and no suspicious-transaction reporting playbook. Staff personal-account dealing is unrestricted. The founders' view, recorded in an email, is that "we are a custodian, not an exchange, so market-abuse rules probably don't bite." That view has not been tested against MiCA Title VI (persons professionally arranging or executing transactions; issuers controlling inside information) or the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook.

9. AML / CFT
A 6-page AML policy skeleton exists. It names CDD tiers and mentions Travel Rule "integration to be selected." There is no business-wide risk assessment, no sanctions-screening vendor, no MLRO, and no SAR procedure. Onboarding of the first design partners has already begun under a "friends and family" exemption invented by the CEO.

10. What this pack is trying to evidence
Aurum believes its client-asset segregation policy, wallet inventory, cold-wallet caps, and MPC key-management design are licensing-ready for a custody review. It does not claim to have a complaints scheme, a reserve attestation, market-abuse controls, a filed white paper, completed authorisation, or a functioning compliance officer. This excerpt is the sole document in the project pack submitted for RegTrace-AI evaluation.
